keepiq/admin-01.title: Set an organisation password policy that the generator and the secret dialogs respect.

decision.reason: Defer: Partial, built, no demand. The missing half is the policy check on the import, extension and write-for-app save paths; no demand row and no competitor yes.

keepiq/admin-02.title: Set the minimum master password strength for everyone.

keepiq/admin-03.title: Approve applications from a queue in the admin settings.

keepiq/admin-04.title: Remove a leaving user from every team folder in one step.

decision.reason: Build: 5 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, 1Password, Passbolt, Keeper, HashiCorp Vault). Specified for the missing half: offboarding also removes the leaver's own team folder member rows; revoking derived shares and handing over owned team secrets is built.

keepiq/admin-05.title: Switch offline caching off for the whole organisation.

keepiq/admin-06.title: Switch breach checking on for the organisation.

keepiq/admin-07.title: Decide how long old versions of secrets are kept.

keepiq/admin-08.title: Create and remove users automatically from a directory through SCIM.

decision.reason: Decided no: Platform capability: vault users are Nextcloud accounts, and accounts are created and removed by Nextcloud's user backends (LDAP, OIDC, SAML or a SCIM provider app). Recorded in docs/FEATURES.md:330 (Nextcloud-native advantages: Nextcloud users and groups are the identity layer, no separate user directory) and :491 (Keepiq inherits Nextcloud identity, SSO and SCIM included). Matrix corrected: provider nextcloud, owner nextcloud/server.

keepiq/admin-09.title: Sync groups from Active Directory or LDAP.

decision.reason: Decided no: owned by nextcloud/server, a platform capability outside the fleet, per the openspec pass addendum: directory groups are synced by Nextcloud's LDAP and AD backend.

keepiq/admin-10.title: Enforce rules such as two-factor login or a ban on exporting personal vaults.

decision.reason: Build: 3 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, 1Password, Keeper). Specified for the vault half: a policy that blocks personal vault export and one that requires Nextcloud two-factor login before the vault unlocks; enforcing two-factor login itself stays Nextcloud's.

keepiq/admin-11.title: Hand out admin roles with only the permissions a person needs.

decision.reason: Build: 4 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, 1Password, Keeper, HashiCorp Vault). Specified for the missing half: named admin roles with a chosen set of permissions; the whole-section delegation and the vault_admin group are built.

keepiq/admin-12.title: See which users have set up a vault.

decision.reason: Build: 4 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, 1Password, Passbolt, Keeper). Specified for the missing half: a list of which users have set up a vault; the count is built.

keepiq/admin-13.title: Manage the organisation through a public admin API.

decision.reason: Build: 4 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, Passbolt, Keeper, HashiCorp Vault).

keepiq/admin-14.title: See the vault's connected integrations and their status in one place.

keepiq/admin-15.title: Set a size limit and a quota for attachments.

keepiq/admin-16.title: See the installed version and its details in the admin settings.

keepiq/admin-17.title: Administrators see pending applications and CA status on the dashboard.

decision.reason: No competitor rated yes, no demand, outside the core area. Reversible: the CA health summary is computed and no widget renders it

keepiq/admin-18.title: An administrator defines new item types and the fields they carry.

decision.reason: Feature request row plus one competitor yes (Keeper); no page creates a type and a type has no field list.

keepiq/admin-19.title: Suspend a user's access and reactivate it later without deleting the account.

decision.reason: Decided no: owned by nextcloud/server, a platform capability outside the fleet, per the openspec pass addendum: suspending and reactivating an account is Nextcloud user management.

keepiq/admin-20.title: Stop ordinary users from browsing the full list of people in the organisation.

decision.reason: Decided no: owned by nextcloud/server, a platform capability outside the fleet, per the openspec pass addendum: who appears in the people picker is set by Nextcloud's sharing settings.

keepiq/admin-21.title: Show every user an announcement, for example about planned maintenance.

decision.reason: Decided no: Platform capability: an announcement to every user is what the Nextcloud Announcement center app provides, and every vault user is a Nextcloud user (the matrix note says so). Matrix corrected: provider nextcloud, owner nextcloud/announcementcenter.

keepiq/admin-22.title: Require that work logins are kept in the organisation's vault rather than in personal vaults.

decision.reason: Build: a tender demand row (https://www.tenderned.nl/aankondigingen/overzicht/295007).

keepiq/admin-23.title: Claim the company's email domain so accounts on it are managed by the organisation.

decision.reason: Decided no: Platform capability: accounts come from Nextcloud's user backends, so which accounts an organisation manages is decided there, not in Keepiq. Recorded in docs/FEATURES.md:330 and :491 (Keepiq inherits Nextcloud identity). Matrix corrected: provider nextcloud, owner nextcloud/server.

keepiq/admin-24.title: An administrator sets the maximum vault timeout that members may choose.

decision.reason: Single competitor, changelog signal only, no demand row

keepiq/admin-25.title: New members are confirmed automatically, without an administrator handing over access by hand.

decision.reason: Build: 3 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, HashiCorp Vault, Nextcloud Passwords).

keepiq/admin-26.title: Administrators see each user's two-factor status and last sign-in in the user list.

decision.reason: Decided no: owned by nextcloud/server, a platform capability outside the fleet, per the openspec pass addendum: each user's last sign-in and two-factor state belong to Nextcloud's user list.

keepiq/admin-27.title: Administrators schedule automatic encrypted backups of every vault on the server and restore them from the command line.

decision.reason: Build: a feature request row (https://community.bitwarden.com/t/adjusting-timezone-and-database-backup-schedule-in-bitwarden/59341) and one competitor yes (Nextcloud Passwords).

decision.reason: Four competitors rate yes; the web auto-lock is a timer from unlock and updateActivity has no caller.
Four competitors rate yes; the timeout choice is not saved and Nextcloud session becomes 10 minutes.

keepiq/crypto-08.title: Unlock the vault with a passkey instead of the master password.

keepiq/crypto-09.title: Unlock with a fingerprint or face scan on your device.

decision.reason: Build: 3 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, 1Password, Keeper). Specified for the missing half: fingerprint or face unlock in the browser extension; the web app unlock with a platform passkey is built.

keepiq/crypto-10.title: Require a second factor such as an authenticator app or security key to open the vault.

decision.reason: Decided no: owned by nextcloud/server, a platform capability outside the fleet, per the openspec pass addendum: a second factor at sign-in is Nextcloud's two-factor login, which gates reaching the vault.

keepiq/crypto-11.title: Let an administrator restore a user's access after a forgotten master password.

decision.reason: Build: 4 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, 1Password, Passbolt, HashiCorp Vault). No recorded non-goal: ADR-005 makes administrator revocation the lost-password route and keeps the server keyless, which an opt-in recovery envelope to an organisation recovery certificate keeps.

keepiq/crypto-12.title: Regain access yourself with a recovery code or kit when the master password is lost.

decision.reason: Defer: Partial, built, no demand. A passphrase backup and emergency access are built; one competitor yes (Keeper) for a recovery kit.

keepiq/crypto-13.title: See which algorithms and key sizes protect your vault.

decision.reason: Build: 3 competitors rate yes (1Password, Passbolt, Keeper).

keepiq/crypto-14.title: Protect each user's vault key with a certificate issued by the instance's own private authority.

keepiq/crypto-15.title: Creating a key never mints a second active one while the first is in use.

keepiq/crypto-16.title: Re-encrypted data is verified before the original is discarded.

keepiq/crypto-17.title: Revoke a user's vault key and reinstate it later.

keepiq/crypto-18.title: An administrator can force-revoke a key flagged as compromised.

keepiq/crypto-19.title: Log in to the vault with single sign-on from the organisation's identity provider.

decision.reason: Decided no: owned by nextcloud/server, a platform capability outside the fleet, per the openspec pass addendum: single sign-on is Nextcloud's login (user_saml, user_oidc); the vault still unlocks with the master password or a passkey.

keepiq/crypto-20.title: Ask for the master password again before a sensitive item is shown or filled.

decision.reason: Build: 2 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, Passbolt).

keepiq/crypto-21.title: See where you are signed in and end a session on another device.

decision.reason: Decided no: owned by nextcloud/server, a platform capability outside the fleet, per the openspec pass addendum: sessions and app passwords are listed and ended in Nextcloud's Devices and sessions.

keepiq/crypto-22.title: Item names, website addresses and usernames are encrypted too, so the server sees no item metadata.

decision.reason: Decided no: Recorded design decision: openspec/specs/secrets/spec.md:14 ('Only the secret's name and URL are stored in plain text to allow listing and searching without decryption') and :566 ('url is stored unencrypted by design, it enables search and Nextcloud unified search integration'). Usernames are already encrypted. Four competitors rate yes and a changelog row exists, so this is flagged for review.

keepiq/crypto-23.title: Lock a user out after repeated failed sign-in attempts.

decision.reason: Decided no: owned by nextcloud/server, a platform capability outside the fleet, per the openspec pass addendum: sign-in throttling and lockout are Nextcloud's brute-force protection and Password policy app.

keepiq/crypto-24.title: Approve a sign-in on a new device from a device where you are already signed in, or have an administrator approve it.

decision.reason: Build: 3 competitors rate yes (Bitwarden, Passbolt, Nextcloud Passwords).

thematiq/gov-no-public-cdn.title: Use the brand center and its branding governance without publishing brand assets on a public content delivery network.

decision.reason: Partial, built, with a changelog demand row (Tokens Studio 2.12.1) and Tokens Studio rated yes. The missing half is authoring a deprecation with a replacement and a removal date; thematiq only reads one on import.

thematiq/sco-per-app-exclude.title: Exclude individual apps from the house style and leave them stock while you test.

thematiq/sco-per-app-login.title: Give each connected application its own branded login page, falling back to the default brand for anything it does not set.

decision.reason: Recorded decision: openspec/specs/per-group-theming/spec.md:56 requires login pages to resolve to the instance default set, so a login page per connected application is excluded.

thematiq/sco-per-domain.title: Show a different brand depending on which domain the user arrives on.

decision.reason: Recorded non-goal: openspec/changes/archive/2026-07-23-per-group-theming/design.md:29 names per-domain mapping as a non-goal (the domain theming app's territory).

thematiq/sco-per-group.title: Give a group of users a different house style on a shared instance.

thematiq/sco-per-site.title: Give each site, portal or department its own theme.

decision.reason: Partial, built, two competitors yes, so a gap; the missing half (a department's public pages, share links and login carrying its own brand) is excluded by openspec/specs/per-group-theming/spec.md:56, which requires anonymous, public-share, login and error pages to resolve to the instance default. The group half stays built.

thematiq/sco-suite-wide-appearance.title: Respect a user's light or dark choice from the central portal in every application of the suite.

decision.reason: Partial, built, with a roadmap demand row (openDesk baseline requirements); the Nextcloud half is built. The missing half is a separate office editor and chat server, which thematiq cannot reach: its CSS injection only reaches same-origin Nextcloud pages (Collabora runs in a separate-origin frame), so that half belongs to those products.

thematiq/sco-tenant-isolation.title: Run fully separate brands for separate tenants on one installation.

decision.reason: Single competitor rated yes (Liferay DXP), no demand row, outside the core area (catalogue and apply). Was defer, retired.

thematiq/sco-user-choice.title: Let each user choose a theme (light, dark, high contrast) for themselves.

thematiq/sco-user-follow-os.title: Follow the user's operating system preference for dark mode and high contrast.

thematiq/sur-all-pages.title: Style every Nextcloud page, including apps from other vendors, not only a single portal.

thematiq/sur-assistant-logo.title: Show the organisation's logo as an approved mark inside the AI assistant, so users can see the assistant is the one their organisation sanctioned.

decision.reason: Roadmap demand (Microsoft 365 roadmap 555852) plus one competitor yes (Microsoft 365). The fleet assistant is CnAiCompanion in nextcloud-vue; thematiq owns the brand setting and publishes the approved mark, nextcloud-vue renders it (sibling half named in the proposal).

thematiq/sur-block-page.title: Brand the page users see when the network blocks a site, with the organisation's own text and links to its policies and IT help.

decision.reason: Owner corrected to external: the row's own evidence says a block page served by a network gateway is not a Nextcloud page, so it is outside the product.

thematiq/sur-component-bridge.title: Map community component tokens (Utrecht) onto the workspace's own components.

thematiq/sur-conduction-apps.title: Have every Conduction app pick up the house style through shared tokens.

thematiq/sur-coverage-report.title: See, per component of the suite, whether the logo, the brand colours and the profile picture actually follow the central theme, so gaps are visible before users find them.

decision.reason: No competitor rated yes, one featureRequest demand row but no competitor yes cell, outside the core area (catalogue and apply). Was defer, retired.

thematiq/sur-custom-domain.title: Serve the branded workspace on the organisation's own domain name.

thematiq/sur-email.title: Send notification emails in the house style.

thematiq/sur-email-footer.title: Add a compliance footer (organisation name, address, legal text) to every email.

thematiq/sur-error-contrast.title: Keep error and status messages readable in every house style.

thematiq/sur-footer-links.title: Add legal links (privacy statement, imprint, accessibility statement) to the footer and login page.

thematiq/sur-generated-documents.title: Have documents the system generates (letters, PDF exports, reports) carry the house style: logo, cover, footer and fonts.

decision.reason: Tender demand (TenderNed 404703, 415897, 298070). Thematiq owns the house style; the change specifies the house style profile that the fleet document generators (filinq huisstijl, openregister PDF export) read, and names their halves.

thematiq/sur-header-nav.title: Style the header and app navigation bar in the house style.

thematiq/sur-help-links.title: Point the help and documentation links in the user menu at the organisation's own documentation.

decision.reason: Owner corrected to nextcloud/server: the help and documentation links are built by core ThemingDefaults (docBaseUrl), and the demand row is a request against nextcloud/server (issue 58909).

thematiq/sur-hide-slogan.title: Hide the Nextcloud slogan on the login page.

thematiq/sur-localised-name.title: Show the instance name and slogan in the user's own language.

decision.reason: Owner corrected to nextcloud/server: the instance name and slogan are single core ThemingDefaults values, and the demand row is a request against nextcloud/server (issue 37550). Thematiq could only change them by rewriting the rendered core page from a script, which breaks with every core release.

thematiq/sur-login-page.title: Style the login page, including before any session exists.

thematiq/sur-login-wording.title: Change the wording on the login page, such as the label of the account field.

decision.reason: Owner corrected to nextcloud/server: the login form and its labels are core, and the demand row is a request against nextcloud/server (issue 38831). Thematiq could only change the labels by rewriting the core login view from a script, which breaks with every core release.

thematiq/sur-menu-labels.title: Show text labels instead of icons only in the app menu.

thematiq/sur-mobile-desktop-clients.title: Carry the brand into the desktop and mobile sync clients.

decision.reason: Owned by nextcloud/server in the matrix: the official clients read core theming capabilities; platform-provided, outside the fleet.

thematiq/sur-nc-variable-mapping.title: Map every Nextcloud colour variable to a design token, so no stock colour leaks through.

thematiq/sur-office-suite.title: Carry the brand into the integrated office editor and chat in the same suite.

decision.reason: No competitor rated yes, no demand row, outside the core area (catalogue and apply). Was defer, retired.

thematiq/sur-per-app-brand.title: Give a collaboration or social app of the suite its own brand name, large and small logo and theme colour from a central brand center.

decision.reason: Roadmap demand (Microsoft 365 roadmap 568364) plus one competitor yes (Microsoft 365). Re-read app-token-set-selection: it lets a leaf app's own picker choose a set for its users, not an admin give an app its own colour and logos, so the row stays none.

thematiq/sur-public-pages.title: Style public share and link pages that visitors without an account see.

thematiq/sur-selection-colour.title: Have selected and highlighted text take the brand colour in a readable, translucent form.

thematiq/sur-status-tokens.title: Colour success, warning and error states from the house style's status tokens.

thematiq/sur-support-link.title: Add a support or helpdesk link next to the legal notice and privacy links.

decision.reason: Owner corrected to nextcloud/server: the legal notice and privacy links are core ThemingDefaults footer links, a third link needs core, and the demand row is a request against nextcloud/server (issue 39047). Thematiq's own email footer could carry one later.

thematiq/sur-web-app-name.title: Change the product name, slogan and web address shown to users.
